registration: Commit before source learner, actor/noise simulator, tests and any benchmark scores. If results fail, document failure without retuning; future modifications need a NEW protocol and NEW seed cohorts.
question: Can learned archive-versus-recent predictive contrast prevent false reversion on neutral samples while sustaining short-latency reacquisition through same-schema A->B->A->B, with imperfect reported public feedback?
environments: Same deterministic engineered two-field range simulator (inlet/outlet), action frame names and candidate distribution unchanged. Hidden A is source and returned A; hidden B reverses progress/damage; all phases produce real simulator outcomes and unlabelled public feedback. NOT new independently authored rules or stochastic physical dynamics.
observation_corruption: After independent random first-action TRAIN outcome, deterministically hash (seed, episode index, 'report-noise') to flip progress<->damage in 10% of episodes where actual outcome is progress or damage; neutral never flipped. Corrupted public feedback is all learner sees. Count both TRUE actor harm and reported damage separately; do not use true effect in learner. TEST is true deterministic hidden outcome, never corrupted.

model.anchor: First 192 events train source relation; 240-source warmup is intentionally provided before hidden changes.
model.entry_to_recent: While archive selected, require at least 2 of latest 4 public outcome classes to have smoothed archive prediction p < 0.125. Only check starting at index 240, without stage markers.
model.archive_reentry: While recent selected, consider latest four public events and a recent-32 alternative fitted on PRECEDING events, excluding the latest four. Require at least two individual events with archive probability >=0.55 AND archive probability >=4 * the alternative probability. Require >=8 events since entering recent to enable comparison. This is discriminatory evidence, not 'absence of surprise' and neutral agreement cannot trigger reentry.
model.recent_horizon: Use recent8 until >=24 observed outcomes have accumulated since the algorithm-inferred switch to recent; then use recent32. No simulator phase label passed. Candidate training overlaps incoming evidence; not fully independent.
model.restart: Append-only validated public observations only, recompute inferred mode/change indices by deterministic event replay; SHA256 exact checkpoint validation. Persist no simulator hidden rules, stage IDs or real-world permissions.
model.abstentions: None. All attempted interventions scored for harmful TEST actions.

metrics: source-actor actual damaging interventions counted once
acceptance: At B1/ B2 8 observations aim >50% successes, at B1/B2 32 and 64 target >=100/120 each, return-A8 >=100/120. Disclose all baselines, false reversion, harm and test metrics even when failure; no promotion even if all gates pass.
cautions: Handcrafted dynamic inversion, manually selected windows/thresholds and deterministic label flips; NOT independent noisy real-world physics, broad transfer, or generalized self-improvement.
B warmup and returning A are structurally easy, and fixed recent32 is a strong benchmark.
Observation forgery remains possible; SHA256 does not authenticate sources.
Source actor causes harmful simulated actions; learner does not intervene to collect data.
No test feedback used for learning and no changing thresholds after seed inspection.
No default agent promotion, GitHub merge, AthenZ/Synveil integration or change to D1-D10/V2A/V2B roadmap.
